name: Marble Bath
author: TBIT DESIGN - Thomas Breher
description: Classic paper marbling on a virtual water bath recreates the art of Ebru and Suminagashi with exact mathematical gestures. You actually marble: drop ink onto the water and watch every earlier drop yield into rings, hold a drop to let it grow, drag to scatter a trail. Then pull tools through the bath and the ink follows physically: a NEEDLE draws a single flowing line, a COMB pulls the whole bath into feathered ripples, a WAVE sways the water into chevrons, a CURL plants a vortex that winds the colours around itself. Every gesture is one move in the bath's history - undo simply forgets the last one, and because the mathematics is exact, the picture stays razor sharp at any export size, with no simulation grid and no blur. EBRU FLOWERS bloom under your hand: click to plant a tulip, carnation or daisy - rings pulled into petals by the needle, with a leafy stem - then drag to turn and size it before letting go. The GALL DROP (ox gall in the real workshop) pushes every colour aside and leaves open water: cells in the pattern, or windows onto your design. An ARC and a RING COMB pull curved strokes and whole concentric medallions, a SPLATTER flick sprays a fan of tiny droplets. And the ink itself now behaves like pigment: a darker rim gathers at every drop's edge, faint clouds drift inside it and stretch with the combing (computed exactly, in the drop's own pre-image), over a faint paper tooth. Classic patterns come as seeded recipes over YOUR inks - Stone, Gel-git, Nonpareil, Chevron, Bouquet, French curls, Peacock - each a starting point you keep marbling on top of. Five ink wells and the water colour are yours to set, brand colours load with one click, and recolouring an ink recolours the finished marbling. CLEAR WATER marbles the veins straight over your design as a transparent overlay. The film export replays the making - drops pattering in, combs sweeping through - or rocks the finished bath on living water as a seamless loop, as a ready video file for download or the Media Library. Inserted as a re-editable generator layer: reopen it any time and the full history is still there, every move still undoable. Everything is computed in your browser - no server, no upload, no account. Fluid Lab is a continuously running second mode with water-based ink, thin oil, thick oil, a separate reflective liquid-metal phase, alcohol and surfactant additives. Twenty-two experiments provide starting points. Stir, pour, blow air, form vortices or place obstacles. Viscosity, metal cohesion and local surface-tension effects change the simulated flow; alcohol evaporates while its dye remains in the water. Smooth reconstructed surfaces show reflections, transmission and oil-film iridescence. Save or reopen the complete experiment, capture the wet surface or a flat paper print as PNG, or record a short video while the bath keeps evolving. Fluid Lab uses a shallow artistic model and requires WebGL2; it does not model volumetric sinking or calibrated chemical reactions.
